boards.title: Your First Weekend at Siena University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe campus sequence for getting oriented, meeting people, and finding recurring Siena activities.

cards.title: 1. Start with Student Activities
cards.subtitle: Sarazen Student Union, Room 302
cards.notes: Stop by or contact Student Activities to identify a weekend program or club that fits your interests, then use its guidance to make a simple first plan.
cards.short_summary: Begin with the office that connects students to campus programs and organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Siena says Student Activities supports campus involvement and that more than 90 clubs and organizations are available.
cards.source_title: Student Activities and Leadership Development | Siena University
cards.access_notes: Office meetings are available by appointment; confirm program details through Siena before attending.

cards.title: 2. Share a meal at Lonnstrom
cards.subtitle: Main campus dining facility
cards.notes: Invite a hallmate or orientation acquaintance to a meal and use the time to compare schedules, campus questions, and one activity you might try together.
cards.short_summary: A practical meet-up point for a first campus meal.
cards.evidence_claim: Siena identifies Lonnstrom Dining Hall as its main dining facility and lists meal plans that provide access there.
cards.access_notes: Dining access depends on a meal plan or other payment arrangement; check current dining service information.

cards.entity_name: J. Spencer and Patricia Standish Library
cards.title: 3. Locate Standish Library
cards.subtitle: Academic Quad
cards.notes: Walk through the three-floor library and note the Writing Center on the bottom floor so you know where to return when coursework starts.
cards.short_summary: Find a central academic resource before classes get busy.
cards.evidence_claim: Siena describes Standish Library as a three-floor library in the Academic Quad and says its Writing Center is on the bottom floor.
cards.access_notes: The accessibility map lists front-entry access, elevator service to all floors, and accessible bathrooms on floors one through three.

cards.entity_name: St. Mary of the Angels Chapel
cards.title: 4. Pause at St. Mary of the Angels Chapel
cards.subtitle: Campus chapel
cards.notes: If quiet reflection or worship appeals, take a respectful look at the chapel and check the Chaplain’s Office for the current liturgy and program schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus place for reflection and Chaplain’s Office programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Siena’s Chaplain’s Office invites students to worship at liturgies or participate in faith-formation programs at St. Mary of the Angels Chapel.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to chapel scheduling and the Chaplain’s Office; private prayer is permitted for Siena community members when it is not in use.

cards.title: 5. Take a quiet Grotto walk
cards.subtitle: Near St. Mary of the Angels Chapel
cards.notes: Make this a short daylight reset: visit respectfully, take in the memorial details, and head back toward the main campus when you are ready.
cards.short_summary: A documented campus space for contemplation and remembrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Siena describes the Grotto as a sacred space for prayer, contemplation, healing, and peace, with several statues and a veterans memorial connection.
cards.access_notes: Visit respectfully and follow any posted campus guidance; no admission information is stated on the source page.

cards.title: 6. Find the Marcelle Athletic Complex
cards.subtitle: MAC, including the UHY Center
cards.notes: Walk over with a friend to identify the gym, pool, courts, track, and UHY Center, then check Athletics for current recreation and facility access details.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented to Siena’s major athletics and recreation complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Siena says the Marcelle Athletic Complex includes a gym, swimming pool, racquetball and squash courts, elevated track, and four basketball courts.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and programming vary; the accessibility map identifies Lot W entrances and accessible bathrooms on all floors via the main-lobby elevator.

cards.title: 7. Spot Beaudoin Theatre
cards.subtitle: Foy Hall
cards.notes: Find the theatre in Foy Hall and watch Siena’s Creative Arts channels for a scheduled performance, audition, or production opportunity that suits your weekend.
cards.short_summary: Know where Siena’s main-stage performances take place.
cards.evidence_claim: Siena identifies Beaudoin Theatre in Foy Hall as its main-stage performance space.
cards.access_notes: Performance availability and any ticketing depend on the specific production; confirm details with Creative Arts.

cards.title: 8. Make the Union your evening hub
cards.subtitle: Sarazen Student Union (SSU)
cards.notes: Use the Union as a meet-up point, check the welcome desk for campus information, and look for a currently scheduled, under-21-friendly program.
cards.short_summary: A central student-services and activity hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Siena describes the Sarazen Student Union as a central hub and says its welcome desk provides event information, directions, and other general information.
cards.source_title: Student Activities and Leadership Development | Siena University
cards.access_notes: Welcome Desk hours listed by Siena are Monday–Friday, noon–6 p.m.; program access varies by event.

cards.title: 9. Choose a Siena Night Life program
cards.subtitle: Recurring programs in the Sarazen Student Union
cards.notes: Check the current campus calendar, then join a listed trivia, craft, or other Siena Night Life program with classmates rather than planning around assumptions.
cards.short_summary: A recurring, under-21-appropriate weekend program series.
cards.evidence_claim: Siena states that Siena Night Life runs every weekend in the Sarazen Student Union, including trivia nights and craft nights.
cards.source_title: Student Activities and Leadership Development | Siena University
cards.access_notes: Siena confirms the programs recur every weekend but does not publish a universal late closing time on this page; verify the specific event listing.

cards.title: 10. Save SAINTS Connect for next weekend
cards.subtitle: Siena’s campus programs and organizations calendar
cards.notes: Before Sunday ends, browse SAINTS Connect, save one upcoming program, and choose one club or organization to investigate during the next week.
cards.short_summary: Turn a first weekend into a concrete next-campus step.
cards.evidence_claim: Siena identifies SAINTS Connect as a comprehensive calendar of programs and events and a directory of student clubs and organizations.
cards.source_title: Student Engagement & Support Resources | Siena University
cards.access_notes: Use the current listing for event-specific access, timing, and any registration requirements.
